name: Congenital Primary Lymphedema Without Systemic or Visceral Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Congenital Lymphedema

criteria.description: Onset of lymphedema at birth or within the first two years of life
No evidence of systemic or visceral organ involvement
Persistent swelling of the distal limbs consistent with lymphatic dysfunction
Positive family history of primary lymphedema (supportive but not required)
Exclusion of secondary causes of lymphedema such as infection, trauma, or malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital onset lymphedema with persistent limb swelling and exclusion of secondary causes, without systemic or visceral involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and exclusion of secondary causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital unilateral or bilateral lower limb lymphedema
pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects feet and distal legs
searchTerms: one or both legs swollen at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-pitting edema localized to distal extremities
searchTerms: firm swelling in hands or feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Stemmer sign positivity (inability to pinch skin at base of second toe)
searchTerms: unable to pinch skin on toe

common.symptomName: Progressive limb swelling over months to years
common.notes: May worsen with standing or activity

common.symptomName: Skin thickening and hyperkeratosis over affected areas
Mild discomfort or heaviness in affected limbs
searchTerms: feeling of heaviness in arm or leg

common.symptomName: Recurrent cellulitis or erysipelas localized to lymphedematous limb
searchTerms: repeat skin infections in swollen limb
cellulitis in swollen arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Limited joint mobility adjacent to swollen areas
searchTerms: stiff joints next to swollen areas

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb asymmetry with hypertrophy of soft tissues
occasional.notes: May be subtle in early stages

occasional.symptomName: Pitting edema in early infancy before progression to non-pitting

searchTerms: fatigue localized to arm or leg

rare.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to limb disfigurement
rare.notes: May occur in older children or adolescents
searchTerms: mental health issues due to limb appearance

laboratory: Absence of markers for infection or systemic inflammation
imaging: Ultrasound showing subcutaneous tissue thickening without venous obstruction
MRI may reveal dilated lymphatic vessels and soft tissue edema
genetic: Mutations in FLT4 (VEGFR3) gene in some familial cases
Other lymphangiogenesis-related gene mutations may be identified
other: Positive Stemmer sign on physical examination
Exclusion of secondary causes by clinical and imaging evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, surgery or malignancy
Onset later in life rather than congenital
Possible systemic signs depending on cause
Familial congenital lymphedema with FLT4 mutations
Often presents with bilateral lower limb involvement
Venous and lymphatic malformations with limb hypertrophy

redFlags: Rapid progression of limb swelling with systemic symptoms
Signs of infection such as fever, erythema, or warmth over limb
Development of ulcerations or skin breakdown on affected limb
references: Mellor RH, et al. Primary congenital lymphedema: clinical features and genetic causes. J Med Genet. 2019.
International Society of Lymphology. The diagnosis and treatment of peripheral lymphedema: 2020 Consensus Document.
